views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Paper a limited Phase One now, but do not lock in the $40–50B farm-purchase headline or any structural legal changes until Washington cancels the 15 December List 4B tariffs and puts some existing-tariff relief on the table. Keep Huawei and industrial-policy issues off this tranche. Use the November APEC window to test whether Trump will trade a written truce for purchases; if he will not, hold the current posture rather than escalate.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. List 3 is at 25%, List 4A is live at 15% (~$110–125B), Huawei remains on the Entity List with Android/chip supply cut off, and the US still has not decided on the 15 December consumer-goods tranche (timeline 2019-05-10, 2019-05-16, 2019-09-01, 2019-10-11; Lighthizer said Dec 15 is still open). That combination hits the export machine and a national-champion tech firm. Q3 GDP slowed to 6.0% (27-year low), August industrial output was the weakest since 2002, merchandise exports eased ~1.3% over the 180-day window, and CNY broke 7 in August (latest ~7.05, +4.3% vs USD since early May) after the manipulator designation. CPI is rising on African swine fever/pork, so the household cost of living is already under pressure. Reserves are still ~$3.12T and growth is positive, so this is not a financial-stability emergency — hence +0.40, not +0.7–1.0.

Action should stay near zero because escalation would jeopardize the first real pause since May (the mid-October 25%→30% hike was suspended) and because Trump needs a farm-belt win, which is leverage, not a reason to give the farm number away for free. Beijing has already sent goodwill (16-category exemptions; soy/pork excluded from extra retaliation) and MOFCOM has refused to endorse the $40–50B figure, tying any binge to market need and tariff rollback. Committing purchases without matching US tariff movement would be concede_purchases; that is premature while existing duties on ~$360B of our goods remain and Huawei is explicitly outside the pact. Negotiate the text, condition volume on Dec 15 cancellation plus some rollback, and keep structural SOE/tech-transfer issues for later phases.
key_factors: Phase One is in principle only: unsigned, 3–5 weeks to paper, Dec 15 List 4B still undecided
Huawei Entity List and US chip/Android cutoff remain outside any deal
Existing US tariffs still cover ~$360B of Chinese goods (List 3 at 25%, List 4A at 15%)
Q3 GDP 6.0% (27-year low), August IP weakest since 2002, exports slightly down
CNY broke 7; US manipulator label; CPI rising on pork/ASF
US political need for farm purchases before 2020 gives China bargaining power
Beijing already offered limited exemptions; MOFCOM has not confirmed $40–50B

sources_cited.excerpt: After Washington talks, Trump announces a "Phase One" deal in principle: China to buy roughly $40–50B of US agricultural products annually; planned mid-October tariff hike delayed.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator.
China announces first tariff-exemption list for some US products (16 categories; industrial inputs / chemicals).
China industrial production index 104.7 in Oct 2019 (down from 106.3 in June); growth slowed through the summer.
China merchandise exports eased from $210.5B (Jun) to $207.7B (Oct), about -1.3% over the window.
China reserves ex-gold still ~$3.12T in Oct 2019; only a modest ~0.4% decline — no reserve crisis.
Tariff hike on ~$250B suspended; Lighthizer said no decision yet on Dec 15 consumer-goods tariffs; Huawei not addressed.
China has not confirmed the $40–50B farm figure; Gao Feng said purchases would follow market needs; Beijing wants existing and future tariffs cancelled for a final deal.
Q3 2019 GDP growth 6.0%, slowest in nearly 30 years; trade war, weak auto demand, and swine fever cited as drags.
